meta.description: Quantifies CRISPR editing outcomes with CRISPResso2 across Cas9-nuclease (indels, HDR), CBE/ABE base editors, and prime editor modes; covers single-amplicon, batch, pooled, WGS off-target, and comparison workflows plus quantification-window math and failure-mode diagnosis.
meta.note: 9 inputs: the pre-fix audit's 7 inputs re-run as regression tests (indices 1-7) plus 2 new auditor-added inputs (8-9) per the re-audit brief.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated statistics, DOIs, or trial results across any of the 9 outputs; all reported percentages trace to real CRISPResso2 2.3.4 Docker runs on real published test FASTQs, independently reproduced this pass.

practice_boundaries.detail: Research-scope amplicon quantification only; no diagnostic or prescriptive claims about a person or patient.

methodological_ground.detail: Quantification-window sizing and the substitution-vs-indel diagnostic are methodologically sound; independently confirmed correct on both the CBE (Input 2) and ABE (Input 9, new) code paths against the same known-Cas9 ground-truth sample.

code_usability.detail: The previously-vetoing parse_crispresso() function was transcribed verbatim from the fixed SKILL.md and run against real CRISPResso2 output (Input 6): it now completes without error and every value (reads_in_input=250, reads_aligned=235, mapping_pct=94.0, Modified%=26.38297872) is correct. The independently-found shipped-script bug (CRISPRessoCompare's old --crispresso_output_folder_1/_2 flags) is also fixed and was run end-to-end (Input 8): exit 0, real comparison output produced.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 4/4 (all 5 CRISPResso2 modes + HDR/CBE/ABE/PE). Correctness now 3/4 (was 2/4 pre-fix): parse_crispresso() and CRISPRessoPooled's default threshold are both fixed and independently verified against real output. Docked 1 point: CRISPRessoWGS remains completely unexecuted across both audit passes (no small-genome reference FASTA cached) -- flag names were re-verified via --help only.

reliability.note: Failure Modes table now covers both the graded '<50% aligned' case and the hard-crash total-failure case (verified: CRITICAL/No alignments found/exit 1/no output folder, reproduced exactly). CRISPRessoPooled's all-NA trap is now documented and the fix (--min_reads_to_use_region 100) reproduces upstream's exact expected percentages. Docked 1 point: no bundled automated test/assertion accompanies the one Python code sample -- correctness still rests on the auditor re-running it by hand each time.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md ~390 lines with usage-guide.md and examples/ split out; reasonable disclosure with minor duplication between the two docs' mode cheat-sheets (unchanged from pre-fix).

agent_usability.note: Mode decision tree and output-file tables are clear and now internally consistent (the mapping-stats-table-vs-Python-snippet contradiction, P2 pre-fix, is resolved -- both now agree the file has no percentage column). Error Prevention improved substantially: both P0s and both P1s from the pre-fix audit are fixed and independently reproduced. Docked 1 point: still no explicit escape-hatch guidance for when to stop and consult a human beyond the failure-mode tables.

human_usability.note: Natural researcher-phrased trigger examples throughout usage-guide.md; the underlying CLI fails loudly and clearly on badly mismatched input (re-verified), which is correct behavior for this domain.

security.note: No hardcoded secrets or injection vectors; all user input is sequence strings and file paths passed as CLI arguments. Minor: no mention of handling patient-derived-sample sensitivity if pointed at clinical amplicon data (unchanged from pre-fix).

maintainability.note: Clean SKILL.md/usage-guide.md/examples split (Modularity 4/4). Testability substantially improved: the bundled Python sample and the bundled shell script both now run correctly against real CRISPResso2 output, independently re-verified this pass rather than taken on the fix log's word. Docked 1 point: still only one code sample total, and it still has no bundled unit test.

agent_specific.note: Strong, precise triggering; correct progressive-disclosure layering; explicit, clean Related-Skills composability with base-editing-analysis, prime-editing-screens, and library-design. Escape Hatches docked slightly, same as pre-fix.

Without the flag: 235/250 aligned, 26.38297872% Modified, byte-identical to upstream's expected result. With the flag (as the Skill's own worked example specifies): 221/250 aligned, 24.88687783% Modified -- exactly the shift SKILL.md now discloses in its own text ('235->221', '26.38%->24.89%').

The substitution-vs-indel diagnostic is correct on both the CBE and the newly-tested ABE code paths (Inputs 2 and 9), consistently identifying the same known-Cas9 sample as non-clean-BE.
All five CRISPResso2 modes have correct, --help-verified CLI flags; four of five (CRISPResso, CRISPRessoBatch, CRISPRessoPooled, CRISPRessoCompare) have live, reproduced execution evidence this pass.

recommendations.title: CRISPRessoWGS remains unexecuted across two audit passes
recommendations.problem: No live run of CRISPRessoWGS exists in either the pre-fix or this re-audit; only --help flag verification.
recommendations.root_cause: No small-genome reference FASTA is cached alongside the audit's small-genome BAM, and building one is out of scope for a time-boxed audit pass.
recommendations.fix: Cache a minimal reference FASTA (matching the existing Both.Cas9.fastq.smallGenome.bam's chr9/chr11 slices) alongside the other test fixtures so a future audit can execute CRISPRessoWGS for real rather than checking flags only.

recommendations.title: Single bundled Python code sample has no accompanying automated test
recommendations.problem: parse_crispresso() only gets verified when an auditor manually re-runs it by hand; nothing in the Skill package would catch a future regression on its own.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill ships documentation and CLI examples but no test harness.
recommendations.fix: Consider adding a minimal pytest-style smoke test (or at least a runnable __main__ block, as this audit's own run/input6_parse_output/test_parse_crispresso.py demonstrates) that future contributors can run before shipping a change to the parser.
